title: C482/422/2010 of BISHMVARI DEVI AND ORS Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND AND ORS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Misc. Application (C-482) No. 422 of 2010
Bishmvari Devi and others ....... Applicants
 versus
State of Uttarakhand & others ....... Respondents
Mr. Kurban Ali, Advocate for the applicants.
Mr. S.S. Adhikari, Brief Holder for the State / respondents no. 1 to 3.
None present for respondent no. 4.
U.C. Dhyani, J.(Oral)

The applicants, by means of present
application / petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., seek
to quash the summoning order dated 07.04.2010, passed
in criminal case no. 1733 of 2009, State of Uttarakhand
vs Sanjay Diwedi, under Section 498-A of IPC and
Section 3⁄4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, pending before
the court of Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kotdwar.
2) Taking recourse to Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C.,
informant (respondent no. 4 herein) lodged an FIR on
21.05.2009, at police station, Kotdwar, District Pauri
Garhwal against four accused persons, including the
applicants, for the offences punishable under Section
498-A of IPC and 3⁄4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act. After
the investigation, charge-sheet was submitted only
against Sanjay Diwedi, who was the husband of
respondent no. 4 for the offences punishable under
Section 498-A of IPC and 3⁄4 of the Dowry Prohibition
Act. No case was found to have been made out against
the other accused persons, namely, Bishmvari Devi

2
(mother-in-law), Anusuya Prasad jeth (brother-in-law)
and Km. Kalpana nanad (sister-in-law). Proceedings of
the criminal case started on the basis of said charge-sheet.
3) When PW1 Suman Diwedi (respondent no. 4
herein) entered into the witness box, she supported
prosecution version. In other words, PW1 reiterated what
was got written by her in her FIR. She also stated a few
things against her mother-in-law, brother-in-law and
sister-in-law in her examination-in-chief. After her
evidence, PW1 moved an application under Section 319
of Cr.P.C. before Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Kotdwar for summoning her mother-in-law, brother-in-law and sister-in-law. Being satisfied with the
sufficiency of reasons given in application under Section
319 of Cr.P.C., present applicants were summoned to
face the trial under Sections 498-A of IPC and 3⁄4 of the
Dowry Prohibition Act, vide impugned order dated
07.04.2010. Aggrieved against the same, present
application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. was moved.
4) Respondent no. 4 was issued notice, but none
turned up for her, despite service of notice through her
counsel.
5) The background of summoning of present
applicants has been given in the foregoing paragraph. Let
us see what was said by PW1 against the present
applicants in her evidence?

3
6) PW1 said, " ..........after about a week or ten
days, my husband Sanjay, mother-in-law Bishmvari
Devi, brother-in-law Anusuya Prasad and sister-in-law
Kalpana started harassing me and demanded a
motorcycle and gold earrings for my mother-in-law. All
of them assaulted me ........... Thereafter, my husband,
mother-in-law, brother-in-law and sister-in-law continued
to harass me for the demand of dowry. Whenever my
father counselled them, they told that you (PW1) would
not be permitted to enter the matrimonial home of your
daughter till the demand of motorcycle is met.......... I
was brought to my matrimonial home, but my husband,
mother-in-law, brother-in-law and sister-in-law continued
to assault and harass me for demand of dowry......... I
remained at my matrimonial home Shivrajpur during the
period April 2006 to August 2006. My husband
proceeded to join his duty at Noida after my
marriage........... My sister-in-law was studying in class
X or XI......... I told before the Helpline that I want to
live with my husband (separately from his other family
members)......... The witness was read over her
statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., in which she was
posed a question as to whether she suspected illicit
relations between her husband and her jethani (sister-in-law)? She replied in the affirmative. This was the reason
I (PW1) want to live separately with my husband..........
After one week of the death of my jethani (sister-in-law),
my husband dropped me at my parental home, saying that
he would be coming back within 2-3 days, but he did not

4
come............." Her husband is not the applicant before
this Court.
7) Learned counsel for the applicants drew the
attention of this Court towards the compromise, which
took place between the parties on 28.04.2008 before
Women Helpline. The husband (not an applicant before
this Court) promised that he will behave properly with his
wife and shall shoulder her responsibility. The wife, on
the other hand, also promised to treat her husband with
respect. The wife also promised that she would behave
properly with her mother-in-law, jeth (brother-in-law)
and nanad (sister-in-law). At that time her jethani (sister-in-law) was alive. Again, the husband wrote an
application to the Inspector In-Charge, police station,
Kotdwar regarding ill-behaviour of his wife, as a
consequence of which, his sister-in-law (wife of his elder
brother) committed suicide on May 8, 2008. Learned
counsel for the applicants further contended that the
nanad (sister-in-law) of respondent no. 4 was only
studying in class X or XI and, therefore, she had no guts
to misbehave with her bhabhi on the pretext of non-fulfillment of demand of dowry. Jeth (brother-in-law)
was implicated falsely because, allegedly, his wife was
having illicit relations with the husband of respondent no.
4. It was further argued that the allegations against the
jeth (brother-in-law) and nanad (sister-in-law) were
sweeping in nature and it cannot, therefore, be said that
prima facie any case was made out against them.
Learned Brief Holder for the State, on the other hand,

5
submitted that the mother-in-law was the integral part of
the joint family of the couple [respondent no. 4 alongwith
Sanjay Diwedi (husband)] and, in normal circumstances,
nothing can happen in a joint family without the
concurrence of the mother-in-law, who plays pivotal role
in the day-to-day affairs of a joint family. There is sense
in the said contention of learned Brief Holder for the
State.
8) Learned counsel for the applicants contended
that summoning of the accused-applicants under Section
319 of Cr.P.C. was nothing but abuse of the process of
the court, in as much as the impugned order dated
07.04.2010, whereby the accused-applicants were
summoned to face the trial, was passed contrary to the
scheme of law.
9) It is further contended by learned counsel for
the applicants that learned Addl. Chief Judicial
Magistrate, Kotdwar ought not have summoned the
applicants under Section 319 of Cr.P.C., on the basis of
the sole testimony of PW1 Suman Diwedi.
10) It was held by Hon'ble Apex Court in
Brindaban Das and others vs State of West Bengal,
(2009) 2 SCC (Cri) 79 that the power under Section 319
Cr.P.C. is to be invoked, not as a matter of course, but in
circumstances where the invocation of such power is
imperative to meet the ends of justice. The fulcrum on
which the invocation of Section 319 Cr.P.C. rests is

6
whether the summoning of persons other than the named
accused would make such a difference to the prosecution
as would enable it not only to prove its case but to also
secure the conviction of the persons summoned. It is
only logical that there must be substantive evidence
against a person in order to summon him for trial,
although he is not named in the charge-sheet or he has
been discharged from the case, which would warrant his
prosecution thereafter with a good chance of his
conviction.
11) It was observed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in
Sarojben Ashwinkumar Shah etc. vs. State of Gujarat
and another, 2011 (2) N.C.C. 414 that the power to
proceed against any person, not being the accused before
the court, must be exercised only where there appears
during inquiry or trial sufficient evidence indicating his
involvement in the offence as an accused and not
otherwise. The power conferred upon the court is
although discretionary but is not to be exercised in a
routine manner - In a sense, it is an extraordinary power
which should be used very sparingly and only if evidence
has come on record which sufficiently establishes that the
other person has committed an offence. A mere doubt
about involvement of the other person on the basis of the
evidence led in before the court is not enough. The court
while exercising its power under Section 319 of the Code
must keep in view full conspectus of the case including
the stage at which the trial has proceeded already and the
quantum of evidence collected till then.

7
12) The Hon'ble Apex Court further cautioned in
respect of exercise of jurisdiction under Section 319 of
Cr.P.C. in the case of Sarabjit Singh and another vs
State of Punjab and another, 2009 AIR SCW 4236.
Relevant extract of the judgment is reproduced here-in-below:
"An order under Section 319 of the Code,
therefore, should not be passed only because the
first informant or one of the witnesses seeks to
implicate other person(s). Sufficient and cogent
reasons are required to be assigned by the court so
as to satisfy the ingredients of the provisions.
Mere ipse dixit would not serve the purpose. Such
an evidence must be convincing one at least for
the purpose of exercise of the extraordinary
jurisdiction.
 For the aforementioned purpose, the courts
are required to apply stringent tests; one of the
tests being whether evidence on record is such
which would reasonably lead to conviction of the
person sought to be summoned."
13) It will also be useful to take into account the
possibility of implicating the near relatives of the
husband in matrimonial disputes, as was observed by the
Hon'ble Supreme Court in Preeti Gupta and another vs
State of Jharkhand and another, (2010) 7 SCC 667,
that it is a matter of common experience that most of the
complaints under Section 498-A IPC are filed in the heat

8
of the moment over trivial issues without proper
deliberations. The ultimate object of justice is to find out
the truth and punish the guilty and protect the innocent.
To find out the truth is a Herculean task in majority of
these complaints. The tendency of implicating husband
and all his immediate relations is also not uncommon. At
times, even after the conclusion of criminal trial, it is
difficult to ascertain the real truth. The courts have to be
extremely careful and cautious in dealing with these
complaints and must take pragmatic realities into
consideration while dealing with matrimonial cases. The
allegations of harassment of husband's close relations
who had been living in different cities and never visited
or rarely visited the place where the complainant resided
would have an entirely different complexion. The
allegations of the complaint are required to be scrutinized
with great care and circumspection.
14) In the instant case, on the basis of quality of
evidence adduced by the prosecution, in so far as the
applicants no. 2 and 3 are concerned, it is difficult to hold
with any amount of certainty that the same would, in all
probability, secure the conviction against them. It would,
therefore, be not proper to subject the applicants no. 2
and 3 to trial by invoking the provisions of Section 319 of
Cr.P.C. The same is, however, not true in respect of
applicant no. 1, who is the mother-in-law of respondent
no. 4.

9
15) In view of the above discussion, the
application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. is allowed so far
as it relates to applicants no. 2 and 3 only. Summoning
order dated 07.04.2010, passed in criminal case no. 1733
of 2009, State of Uttarakhand vs Sanjay Diwedi, under
Section 498-A of IPC and Section 3⁄4 of the Dowry
Prohibition Act, pending before the court of Addl. Chief
Judicial Magistrate, Kotdwar are hereby quashed qua
applicants no. 2 and 3 only.
16) At this stage, learned counsel for the applicant
no. 1 prayed that the bail application of applicant no. 1 be
directed to be decided by learned Magistrate on the same
day, subject to her surrender. Keeping in view the fact
that no charge-sheet was submitted against applicant no.
1, after the investigation, and she was summoned under
Section 319 of Cr.P.C. only, after the statements of PW1
were recorded by the trial court, it is provided that if the
applicant no. 1 surrenders before learned Magistrate and
seeks bail, her bail application shall be decided by the
court concerned on the same day.
